title: Choose the visual world for Relo AI
question: The roll assigned the Tear-off Flyer. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Tear-off Flyer
options.lineage: campus bulletin-board 'room for rent' flyers with a fringe of tear-off tabs
options.thesis: Your move plan as the flyer every new grad has torn a tab from: one big number, a fringe of months to tear off.
options.viewport: Left: your situation and chat. Right: the plan, its headline number set huge, with the savings months as a fringe of vertical tear-off tabs along its bottom edge.
options.risk: If the tabs turn decorative instead of working (each tab really marks a month saved), it reads as a costume.

raised.raise: One thing owns the first look: the headline number, alone, at room-reading scale.
Magnitude ramp: each move-in cost is drawn at a size set by its dollar amount on one fixed ramp.
Extent as structure: the cost breakdown is one proportional strip whose segment widths are the amounts.
Integer type steps: one type ramp in fixed steps, nothing sized ad hoc.
Nothing labeled twice: every figure appears once on screen.

options.label: Boarding Pass
options.lineage: airline boarding passes and their tear-off stubs
options.thesis: Your move as a ticket: origin to destination, departs on your date, the fare is what you need to save.
options.viewport: Left: chat. Right: a wide ticket with CHI to SEA, the departure date and the total as the fare; the monthly amount on the stub.
options.risk: Familiar: ticket-styled UIs are a common move in travel and fintech demos.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: Every move ends at a departure board; your plan is the row that clacks into place.
options.viewport: Left: chat. Right: a board with your headline number flipping into place, cost rows below, delayed rows in amber for warnings.
options.case: Holds audience identification strongly; loses on clarity, since all-caps cells slow reading of costs and warnings.
options.risk: All-caps flap text gets hard to read in long warnings.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Costs plotted as stars, size by magnitude.
options.case: Loses both axes: new grads don't identify with star charts, and a sky hides a budget.
options.kept: Magnitude ramp: cost size scales with amount.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.thesis: The plan as a tabbed manual section.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to moving, and its step-only motion fights a live chat.
options.risk: Nostalgia for a product nobody in the audience used.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One plan item per full screen.
options.case: Loses both axes: a projected laptop demo, and a plan read as a whole, not a swipe.
options.kept: One thing owns the first look.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: The headline number in poster-scale pixels.
options.case: Loses both axes: pixel type undercuts trust in money figures.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: The plan as a coded catalog entry.
options.viewport: A black field with one plot.
options.case: Loses both axes: coded labels are the opposite of plain English.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean fintech dashboard, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Chat on the left, KPI tiles and a savings chart on the right.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other fintech demo the judges see that day.
